bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge RTL, message_length was updated using the post-prim_packer handshake and mask: it incremented only when reg_fifo_wvalid && fifo_wready && !hmac_fifo_wsel, and the byte count was derived from reg_fifo_wmask. Because prim_packer can hold partial byte-enabled writes until enough bytes form a full word or until hash_process flushes them, trailing partial writes were not counted when software expected the message length to reflect all bytes written. The root cause is that message-length accounting sampled the data and ready/valid condition after prim_packer instead of at the message-window write entering prim_packer.
bug_info.fix_hint: Move message-length accounting to the input side of prim_packer. Count bytes using the original TL-UL message write mask (msg_fifo_wmask) and enable the update with the packer input acceptance condition (msg_write && sha_en && packer_ready). This ensures every accepted byte-enabled write, including trailing partial writes, increments message_length immediately when it enters the packer, so the reported length is correct before hash_process.
